title: Augmented Computational Design
venue: Artificial Intelligence in Performance-Driven Design: Theories, Methods, and Tools Towards Sustainability
extended_summary:
This chapter proposes Augmented Computational Design (ACD), a framework for using AI in performance-driven generative design. The central problem is how to represent design tasks so that AI can help both evaluate many design alternatives and navigate from desired outcomes back to feasible design decisions. The authors argue that architectural and engineering design should be treated as a discrete decision-making problem, with explicit decision variables and performance indicators, rather than as an ill-defined geometric form-making task.

The approach combines mathematical formulation, dimensionality reduction, and probabilistic modeling. The paper describes design spaces as pairs of decision-space and performance-space vectors, then discusses mapping problems (predicting outputs from inputs) and navigation problems (deriving inputs from desired outputs). It emphasizes the use of interpretable latent spaces, Jacobian-based local linearization, singular value decomposition, and pseudo-inverse reasoning as conceptual tools for explainable AI in generative design.

As a demonstration, the chapter presents a case study from building energy modelling in the Netherlands. The authors approximate the Dutch NTA 8800 building energy calculation model using a shallow Bayesian Belief Network meta-model trained on 20,000 Sobol-sampled simulations across 269 inputs, reduced to 15 influential parameters through sensitivity analysis. The resulting surrogate is intended to support policy analysis and early-stage design by making the model more tractable, more transparent, and more reversible for generative exploration. The conclusion is that AI is most useful in AEC when problems are highly complex, data-driven, and difficult to capture with conventional methods, but that interpretability and feasibility constraints remain important.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual and methodological book chapter with an illustrative engineering case study, not a peer-reviewed experimental or quasi-experimental study of an educational intervention. It provides no K-12 empirical design, no comparison condition, and no outcome estimates relevant to the target topic.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no demonstrated impact on K-12 learning, safety, or science inquiry support outcomes. Its contributions are theoretical and domain-specific to architectural generative design and energy policy modeling.

interventions.use_case: augmented computational design for architectural generative design, using Bayesian Belief Networks as a surrogate/meta-model to map design variables to building energy performance and to navigate from desired outcomes back to design choices

finding.finding_summary: This is a methodological/framework chapter rather than an empirical evaluation of student learning or AI safety outcomes in K-12. It proposes a computational design framework and demonstrates a surrogate model for policy analysis in building energy modelling, but reports no educational intervention effects, no K-12 sample, and no measured learner outcomes.
